title: normalize-token-cost-buckets-and-adaptive-span-sampling
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce normalized token_cost_bucket label with fixed buckets to reduce metrics cardinality; add adaptive trace sampling with higher sampling for error/timeout flows; update Grafana dashboards and tune token-cost alerts to aggregate by service instead of route.
description:
Context and motivation: Our token-level cost and latency metrics have grown high-cardinality over the last year (per-route + per-model + variable token-length labels). This created two problems: Prometheus remote write ingestion costs spiked and some alert rules started firing noisy signals for low-traffic routes. This change introduces a deterministic bucketing strategy for token-level cost and a lightweight adaptive span sampling policy to keep tracing volume stable while increasing capture rate for error/slow paths. Goals: 1) Reduce metrics cardinality and long-term storage costs. 2) Keep token-level observability for SLOs and regression detection. 3) Reduce noisy alerts by moving to aggregated alerting and improved thresholds. 4) Maintain backwards compatibility for dashboards during a deprecation window.

Summary of changes: - Add token_cost_bucket metric label and a deterministic bucketer that maps raw per-request token cost to one of fixed buckets [0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500] micro-units. The runtime now emits token_cost_bucket and token_cost_estimate (capped float) while deprecating the previous free-form token_cost label. - Implement an adaptive span sampler: default sample_rate=0.01 (1%), errors and timeouts sample at min(10%, 10x base) and there's a short-term burst cap to avoid sudden spikes. Sampling decisions are deterministic per-request id to avoid partial traces. - Dashboard updates: Grafana panels replaced route-level noisy charts with aggregated service views; new panels show bucketed distribution and delta-to-baseline. - Alert tuning: switch token-cost SLO alerts from per-route P99 to service-level P99 with a 5% burn window; add a high-cardinality guard alert that triggers if unique label values exceed threshold. - Backwards compatibility: keep old metric token_cost_unbucketed exported for 30 days as a plain counter (no label cardinality growth) and add migration docs. - Tests: unit tests for bucketer edge cases, integration tests for exporter and sampling repeatability; CI runs include short perf bench to detect regression.

Commits (high-level): - 1f2a4d3: runtime: add token_cost bucketer and capped estimate export - 3c9b201: tracing: adaptive span sampler and deterministic decision - 7a8f33b: metrics/exporter: preserve legacy token_cost_unbucketed for deprecation - b2d1a9e: dashboards: grafana panels & migration script - 9d4c8f0: alerts: move token-cost alerts to service aggregation and add cardinality guard - f5e6a11: tests: unit and integration tests + perf smoke - c0d2b6a: docs: observability/token-cost-buckets.md and migration notes

Files touched (high-level): - redwood/observability/metrics/token_cost.go (bucketer + exporter) - redwood/observability/tracing/sampler.go (adaptive sampler) - redwood/observability/exporter/prometheus_exporter.go (label cardinality guards) - dashboards/grafana/token_cost_service_dashboard.json (new panels + migration notes) - docs/observability/token-cost-buckets.md - alerts/rules/token_cost_service_rules.yaml - tests/integration/test_token_cost_bucketing.go - tests/perf/smoke_token_cost_latency.sh - examples/observability/token-cost-demo.sh

Implementation notes and rationale: - Bucket boundaries are intentionally coarse (exponential-ish) to preserve signal for small-cost operations while collapsing long-tail expensive requests into manageable categories. Buckets were tuned using 3 months of production sampled metrics; heuristics included model family and route distributions. - We emit token_cost_estimate (capped to 2 decimals) to allow SLO math where exact per-token micro-cost isn't required. Consumers who need exact accounting can use the separate billing pipeline. - Sampling is deterministic using a stable hash on request_id + service to make sure spans are consistently sampled across downstream processes. Error/timeouts override sampling to increase observability. - To avoid chart breakage, dashboards ship with a compatibility toggle and we preserved legacy panels under a migration folder. - Cardinality guard in the exporter will drop/opportunistically aggregate new label values and increment dropped_label metrics; this helps fast detection of label explosions.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation in runtime exporter and tracer - [x] Unit tests for bucketer and sampler - [x] Integration tests for metric export and trace sampling repeatability - [x] Dashboard updates + migration script - [x] Docs + migration notes - [x] SRE review and alert tuning

Review discussion (condensed): - Marco Li: "Please ensure we don't create a new high-card label — token_cost_bucket is OK but confirm that route/model labels stay bounded." Aisha: "We keep route/model only at service-level aggregation for alerts; exporter enforces label whitelist and drops unexpected labels. added tests." - Brian O'Connor: "Sampler should be deterministic across processes; can we avoid using wall-clock random seeds?" Aisha: "Sampler uses xxhash of request id + service key; added unit tests to verify repeatability." - Svetlana Kuznetsova: "Perf impact?" Aisha: "Bench smoke shows ~2.5% CPU bump in worst case and negligible added tail latency; included perf run in CI and noted numbers in docs." - Marco: "Agree to deprecate old metric after 30 days. Document migration steps." Aisha: "Added docs and migration script, will coordinate dashboard switch with SRE window." - Final: Approved by Marco and Brian after minor nits; Svetlana approved after perf numbers added.

CI summary: - build: passed - lint: passed (two lint nits fixed in follow-up commit) - unit tests: passed - integration tests: flake on first run (prom exporter timeout), rerun passed - perf smoke: passed within expected budget - e2e demo: manual validation performed by SRE
